evaluate.why: a witness the quorum does not name counts for nothing

cases.name: minimal
cases.why: one log, one witness, one quorum

cases.name: no-trailing-newline
cases.why: the final line's newline is optional

cases.name: blank-and-whitespace-lines
cases.why: a line that is empty, or only spaces and tabs, is ignored

evaluate.why: a nested group counts as one member, met as its own threshold decides
inner is `any` of pi and vps

cases.name: nested-group
cases.why: a group may name a group; it counts as one member, satisfied or not

evaluate.why: the log line is not what a quorum is about

cases.name: no-log-line
cases.why: `log` is not required by the grammar: the trust file carries the log key

cases.name: comment-and-indent
cases.why: a line whose first non-space character is `#` is ignored, and leading spaces and tabs are not part of a field

cases.name: bad-vertical-tab
cases.why: only ASCII space and tab separate fields, anywhere in a line

cases.name: bad-duplicate-name
cases.why: a name is defined once

cases.name: bad-forward-reference
cases.why: a group names previously-defined members only

cases.name: bad-two-quorums
cases.why: there is exactly one quorum line

cases.name: bad-no-quorum
cases.why: there is exactly one quorum line

cases.name: bad-empty-group
cases.why: a group has at least one member

cases.name: bad-unknown-keyword
cases.why: every line is one of the four directives

cases.name: bad-quorum-undefined
cases.why: the quorum names something the policy defines

cases.name: bad-duplicate-member
cases.why: no member twice -- `2 of pi pi` is met by one witness

cases.name: bad-k-zero
cases.why: 1 <= k <= n -- k=0 is met by nobody, so an uncosigned head passes

cases.name: bad-k-leading-zero
cases.why: k is canonical decimal: two spellings of a quorum are two policies that look different and are not

cases.name: bad-carriage-return
cases.why: only ASCII space and tab; `bad-vertical-tab` covers only one of the three

cases.name: bad-uppercase-keyword
cases.why: the four directives are lowercase

cases.name: bad-extra-field
cases.why: a directive takes the fields its production allows and no more

cases.name: comment-tab-indented
cases.why: the indent before a `#` is spaces *and tabs*; only-U+0020 reads this line as a directive named `#`

cases.name: bad-trailing-comment
cases.why: `#` after a directive's fields is an ordinary character, so this is a `quorum` line with two names; a reader that strips from `#` accepts it

cases.name: witness-url-fragment
cases.why: a `#` inside a field is content: a reader for which `#` is illegal anywhere refuses a URL with a fragment in it

comment: SPEC 9.1's restated `tlog-policy` grammar, one whole policy per rule, each differing from a valid one in exactly one way. A case with `accept` true MUST parse; the rest MUST be refused. The text is the file verbatim -- some cases turn on whether it ends in a newline. A case with `evaluate` also says what its quorum MEANS: each entry gives a set of cosigner names and whether they satisfy it, which is the only way a reader's arithmetic can be checked
